scenarios.title: Strategy vs Setup Distinction
scenarios.questionText: What fundamentally distinguishes a complete 'Trading Strategy' from a mere 'Trade Setup'?
options: A setup is the visual chart pattern; a strategy includes entry rules, position sizing, invalidation, management, and post-trade review.
A strategy is just any indicator crossing over on the 1-minute chart.
A setup guarantees 100% win rate while a strategy has random outcomes.
They are completely identical terms with no practical difference.
scenarios.correctAnswer: A setup is the visual chart pattern; a strategy includes entry rules, position sizing, invalidation, management, and post-trade review.
scenarios.explanation: A setup is only the conditional trigger. A true strategy governs capital allocation, risk limits, invalidation points, exit plans, and journaling.

scenarios.title: Confluence Definition
scenarios.questionText: Why is 'Confluence' considered the core foundation of high-probability trading?
options: Multiple independent technical factors aligning (structure, key zone, rejection) increases edge and filters low-quality noise.
Confluence eliminates all trading losses permanently.
Confluence means using 15 different indicators that all calculate the same moving average.
It allows you to increase risk to 50% of your account per trade.
scenarios.correctAnswer: Multiple independent technical factors aligning (structure, key zone, rejection) increases edge and filters low-quality noise.
scenarios.explanation: Confluence combines distinct market signals (e.g. Higher Timeframe Trend + Support Zone + Pinbar Rejection) to improve decision quality.

scenarios.title: Invalidation Point Rule
scenarios.questionText: When should a disciplined trader determine their technical invalidation point (Stop-Loss)?
options: Before entering the trade, based on structural market logic where the trade idea is proven false.
After the trade moves 50 pips into drawdown so you can hope for a turnaround.
Never; always hold until the market returns to break-even.
Only when receiving a margin call from the broker.
scenarios.correctAnswer: Before entering the trade, based on structural market logic where the trade idea is proven false.
scenarios.explanation: Pre-defining your structural invalidation level ensures detached risk calculation and prevents catastrophic holding of failing setups.

scenarios.title: The Role of Market Context
scenarios.questionText: Why can an identical bullish engulfing candle succeed in one session and fail in another?
options: Because market context (HTF trend, support vs resistance location, volatility) dictates whether a pattern has genuine edge.
Because candlesticks work by pure random chance with zero pattern logic.
Because market makers only look at retail stop losses on Tuesdays.
Because bullish engulfing patterns only work in stock markets, never forex.
scenarios.correctAnswer: Because market context (HTF trend, support vs resistance location, volatility) dictates whether a pattern has genuine edge.
scenarios.explanation: Location and trend context give candles meaning. A bullish pinbar at major HTF support is high quality; the same pinbar into overhead resistance is low quality.

scenarios.title: Rule-Based Execution
scenarios.questionText: What is the primary benefit of enforcing a strict written rule checklist before order entry?
options: It neutralizes emotional impulses (FOMO, boredom, revenge) and standardizes decision quality.
It guarantees every single trade will hit take profit.
It makes trading fast enough to execute 100 scalps a minute.
It allows you to bypass risk management rules on strong setups.
scenarios.correctAnswer: It neutralizes emotional impulses (FOMO, boredom, revenge) and standardizes decision quality.
scenarios.explanation: Checklists bridge the gap between analysis and execution, preventing impulsive trades driven by emotion rather than pre-planned strategy.

options: It locks in objective risk-to-reward parameters before emotional cognitive bias can interfere.
It allows traders to trade without paying attention to market structure.
It guarantees immediate profit on every setup without drawdown.
It eliminates the need to ever journal trade outcomes.
scenarios.correctAnswer: It locks in objective risk-to-reward parameters before emotional cognitive bias can interfere.
scenarios.explanation: Systematic trade management requires fixed boundary conditions so expectancy can be evaluated statistically across a large sample size.

scenarios.title: Confluence Case #1: Multi-Pillar Assessment
scenarios.questionText: Market Scenario: HTF Trend is Bullish (Aligned), Price is at Major 4H Support Zone, Candlestick shows Bullish Hammer Rejection, R:R is 3.2 : 1. What is the correct confluence rating?
options: High Confluence (85+ Score): Setup satisfies trend, key level, rejection, and 3:1 R:R.
Low Confluence: Avoid trading because high R:R is always a scam.
Medium Confluence: Enter without a stop loss to give it room to breathe.
Random Confluence: Flip a coin to decide position direction.
scenarios.correctAnswer: High Confluence (85+ Score): Setup satisfies trend, key level, rejection, and 3:1 R:R.
scenarios.explanation: All core pillars align: HTF trend continuation, historical key support zone, confirmed hammer wick rejection, and favorable >3:1 R:R.

scenarios.title: Confluence Case #2: Multi-Pillar Assessment
scenarios.questionText: Market Scenario: HTF Trend is Choppy / Conflicted, Price is at Mid-range Air Pocket, Candlestick shows Doji with No Direction, R:R is 0.9 : 1. What is the correct confluence rating?
options: Low Confluence (<50 Score): Conflicted trend, poor location, and sub-1:1 R:R (No Trade).
High Confluence: Enter immediately with 10x leverage regardless of location.
Medium Confluence: Enter without a stop loss to give it room to breathe.
Random Confluence: Flip a coin to decide position direction.
scenarios.correctAnswer: Low Confluence (<50 Score): Conflicted trend, poor location, and sub-1:1 R:R (No Trade).
scenarios.explanation: Lacks multiple necessary pillars: middle of range, unconfirmed candle, negative R:R, and conflicted trend context. Correct action is No Trade.
